original_value: Recent technological advancement in wireless communication has led to the invention of wireless body area networks (WBANs), a cutting-edge technology in healthcare applications. WBANs interconnect with intelligent and miniaturized biomedical sensor nodes placed on human body to an unattended monitoring of physiological parameters of the patient. These sensors are equipped with limited resources in terms of computation, storage, and battery power. The data communication in WBANs is a resource hungry process, especially in terms of energy. One of the most significant challenges in this network is to design energy efficient next-hop node selection framework. Therefore, this paper presents a green communication framework focusing on an energy aware link efficient routing approach for WBANs (ELR-W). Firstly, a link efficiency-oriented network model is presented considering beaconing information and network initialization process. Secondly, a path cost calculation model is derived focusing on energy aware link efficiency. A complete operational framework ELR-W is developed considering energy aware next-hop link selection by utilizing the network and path cost model. The comparative performance evaluation attests the energy-oriented benefit of the proposed framework as compared to the state-of-the-art techniques. It reveals a significant enhancement in body area networking in terms of various energy-oriented metrics under medical environments.

result.paraphrase: Wireless body area networks (WBANs), a modern healthcare technology, have emerged from recent advances in wireless communication. These networks link intelligent, miniaturized biomedical sensor nodes placed on the human body to enable unattended monitoring of a patient’s physiological parameters. The sensors have limited computation, storage, and battery resources. Data communication in WBANs is highly resource intensive, especially in terms of energy. A major challenge is designing an energy-efficient framework for next-hop node selection. To address this, the paper proposes a green communication framework based on an energy-aware, link-efficient routing approach for WBANs (ELR-W). First, it introduces a network model centered on link efficiency that accounts for beaconing information and the network initialization process. Second, it derives a path-cost calculation model focused on energy-aware link efficiency. Using these network and path-cost models, a complete ELR-W operational framework is developed for energy-aware next-hop link selection. Comparative performance evaluation confirms the energy-related advantages of the proposed framework over state-of-the-art techniques, showing significant improvements in body area networking across various energy-oriented metrics in medical environments.
